answer: Local Expansion Impedance Routing. Nodes measure incoming traffic variance from adjacent peers like a steady zephyr before forwarding resources. The network restricts routing bandwidth toward any local cluster where connection density exceeds the regional median pulse by a factor of ten. An attacker adding cheap sybil nodes pays a structural penalty: their isolated subnet faces extreme packet throttling at the network summit, isolating their fake nodes from profitable trade paths and rendering mass replication economically unviable.
